title: Ecology Stratification
definition: Ecological stratification refers to the vertical or horizontal layering of organisms within an ecosystem, driven by the differential availability of resources like light, nutrients, and moisture. It represents the spatial organization of species to minimize inter-specific competition and maximize niche utilization.
importanceInUpsc: UPSC frequently tests the relationship between vertical layering (e.g., rainforests) and biodiversity indices. It is critical for understanding ecosystem stability, niche differentiation, and climate change impacts on forest structure.
learningOutcomes: Master foundational concepts and mechanisms of Ecology Stratification.
Evaluate spatial distribution, institutional frameworks, and policy dimensions.
Apply high-yield mnemonics to solve tricky Prelims and Mains questions.
prerequisites: Core foundational concepts of Niche and Habitat
